title: AMLO Authorizes “Only Morena” to Use His Words and Image, and Calls to Support Sheinbaum
author: SinEmbargo Staff
content:
_This article by[SinEmbargo
Staff](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/redaccion/) originally appeared in the
[October 3, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4881153/amlo-autoriza-solo-a-morena-
usar-sus-palabras-e-imagen-y-pide-apoyar-a-sheinbaum/), a Mexican independent
digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, October 3 (SinEmbargo).—** Former President **Andrés Manuel
López Obrador** (AMLO) exclusively authorized **Morena** to **use his image**
and **his words** for **political and electoral purposes** , in a message
included at the end of his new book _Pueblo_ (2026).

"Morena may use my words and image for political and electoral purposes: no
one else," the former president stated.

In the final chapter, titled "Transition Without Crisis," López Obrador said
farewell from his retirement in Palenque, Chiapas, with three considerations.
In addition to what he said about Morena, he called for voting for the party,
maintaining that it is a "guarantee of well-being for the people," and closed
with a message of support for President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo.

> All of us must support, consciously but without hesitation or pettiness, our
> President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, who has shown, with deeds, that she is an
> exceptional woman and a leader who has fulfilled our simple but transcendent
> political creed of not lying, not stealing and not betraying the people.
>
> Andrés Manuel López Obrador

![López Obrador, seated on a porch, holds up a copy of his book
Pueblo.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/2026-10-03-amlo-morena-words-image-02-pueblo-
book.jpg)López Obrador closed his book _Pueblo_ (2026) with three
considerations addressed to Morena and a message of support for the President
of Mexico. Photo: Screenshot

## AMLO Asks Morena to Avoid Ambitions Ahead of the Upcoming Elections

In the same chapter, the former president addressed the upcoming electoral
processes and called on members of the guinda party to place the movement's
principles ahead of personal aspirations. In that context, he maintained that
the party should not function as a path to obtaining public posts.

"Morena is not only a political party, an office for obtaining posts, but the
main institution of public interest, created by the people for their benefit,
protection and defense," he wrote.

The Morena leader warned that no hopeful should seek a nomination "at any
cost" and called for respecting the polls established in the party's statutes.
He indicated that "unbridled ambition" can end up discrediting those who put
posts, money or power ahead of the movement's principles.

"Finally, in the upcoming elections, let none of you become obstinate and want
to be nominated as a candidate at any cost, without winning a poll, as
Morena's statutes establish, driven by unbridled ambition, without restraining
yourselves," he said.

![President Claudia Sheinbaum speaks from a podium bearing the Mexican coat of
arms.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/2026-10-03-amlo-morena-words-
image-03-sheinbaum.jpg)López Obrador called for backing Claudia Sheinbaum
"without hesitation or pettiness," describing her as an exceptional woman and
a leader committed to the principles of her movement. Photo: Presidencia

He also set limits on the selection of candidates, even when that could mean
losing an election. As an example, he rejected the nomination of the husband
or wife of an outgoing official to replace them, and questioned the choice of
popular figures when there is evidence of unlawful conduct.

"We must always seek a balance between political effectiveness and principles,
but there are limits. If the candidate with whom we can win is the husband or
wife of the official they are going to replace, it is better to lose," he
declared.

Under that same logic, he maintained that internal unity should not be
preserved at the cost of the party's ideals and considered that the departure
of those who have betrayed them does not necessarily harm the movement.

"It is important to remain united, but we also shouldn't believe that the
movement is harmed if we leave Morena after betraying the party's ideals.
Don't forget that by keeping to principles, one wins by losing," he concluded.
